documents.abstract: The most exciting development in nanomedicine is the injectable nanorobots that combine nanotechnology, robotics, biotechnology, materials science, and artificial intelligence for extremely accurate illness detection and treatment. In contrast to conventional drug delivery systems that disperse medication throughout the body, injectable nanorobots are engineered to navigate bodily fluids, detect disease-specific biomarkers, and release therapeutic agents selectively at the target site. These systems have demonstrated significant potential in areas such as cancer, cardiovascular disease, neurological conditions, infectious diseases, regenerative medicine, and precision diagnostics. Recent advancements in enzyme-powered, magnetic, ultrasound-driven, and biohybrid nanorobots have expedited the transfer of these technologies from lab research to preclinical and early translational investigations. Biocompatibility, biodegradability, large-scale production, real-time navigation, regulatory approval, and long-term biosafety are some of the issues that still need to be resolved despite the tremendous advancements. The present understanding of injectable nanorobots, including their historical evolution, classification, structural elements, fabrication techniques, propulsion mechanisms, targeting tactics, biological applications, safety issues, and potential future clinical uses, is compiled in this review. A thorough overview of this quickly developing topic discusses recent developments and new trends.

The spread of generative artificial intelligence in higher education has begun to change writing classrooms in ways that are not always immediately visible. In second language education, students now revise and refine texts through AI-supported interaction before teachers ever see the final product. This shift raises questions not only about writing quality, but also about how teachers understand, evaluate, and guide the writing process itself. In Japanese writing instruction, where revision often depends on close attention to context, nuance, and interpersonal positioning, these changes carry particular weight. This study examines how ten instructors of Japanese writing at Hanoi University perceive the growing presence of generative AI in their teaching. Based on survey data and qualitative interpretation, the analysis shows that writing instruction remains deeply dependent on teacher labor, especially in areas that require contextual judgment and individualized feedback. At the same time, many instructors described a growing sense of uncertainty. When revision happens through AI outside the classroom, it becomes harder to determine what a student can actually do alone, and this weakens confidence in conventional forms of assessment. Some participants also felt that the teacher’s traditional role as the central source of correction is becoming less stable. Yet this did not lead them to view AI as a replacement. Instead, they emphasized that meaning-making in Japanese writing still relies on human sensitivity to social context and rhetorical intention. Rather than simply introducing efficiency, generative AI appears to be changing the balance of authority in writing education itself.

The advancement of digital technology has brought significant changes to economic transaction systems, shfting from conventional face to face transactions to online based transactions. This transformation offers greater convenience and efficiency homever, it also raises various legal issues, practicularly concerning transparency, fairness, and te clarity of information in transactions. From the perspective of Islamic commercial law, this situation has the potential to give rise to elements of gharar due to limitations in direct verification and information asymmetry. This study aims to analyze the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in minimizing gharar in digital transactions. The method used is a qualitative approach with a normative-empirical research design through literature review and interviews with practitioners and academics. The analysis is conducted descriptively-analytically and comparatively between AI practices and Sharia principles. The results indicate that AI plays a role in enhancing transparency through data verification, fraud detection, and real-time information presentation, thereby supporting the principles of bayan, taradi, and hifz al-mal. However, the potential for gharar may still arise if algorithms lack transparency, are biased, or are misused. Therefore, human oversight and Sharia audits are necessary to ensure that the use of AI remains in line with the principles of justice and public interest in Islamic economic transactions.

With the rapid progress of end-to-end digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, big data, the Internet of Things, various digital platforms, etc., there is a need to develop a new approach to learning and education. The purpose of the article is to analyze the possibilities of end-to-end digital technologies in the cycle of educational classes «Conversations about the important» in the educational process of the university. The operational effectiveness of artificial intelligence agents in customer support is frequently attributed to the generative sophistication of underlying language models, although answer reliability primarily depends on the structure and quality of the referenced knowledge base. In complex technical domains such as the Internet of Things (IoT), static documentation alone often fails to resolve customer inquiries that involve real-time device states, sensor readings, and connectivity logs. This study investigates how progressive tiers of knowledge integration affect the response quality of an AI agent within an IoT customer support context. Employing a mixed-method pilot design combining literature synthesis, comparative analysis, experimental testing, and conceptual exploration, thirty representative questions were classified into informational, status, and diagnostic categories. These queries were evaluated across four operational scenarios: without retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), article-based RAG, article plus device metadata records, and a comprehensive hybrid framework integrating static articles, device records, and telemetry streams. Answer quality was measured using Cosine Similarity, BERTScore (F1), and a randomized blind human evaluation assessing relevance, correctness, and usefulness. The results demonstrate that while curated static documentation adequately addresses procedural informational queries, resolving status and diagnostic issues necessitates real-time operational context. The hybrid integration delivered the highest overall performance, achieving a human-evaluation score of 4.40 compared with 2.53 for article-based RAG (p = 0.0039). These empirical findings confirm that robust IoT support agents require dynamic knowledge governance that bridges versioned documentation, synchronized asset metadata, and live telemetry data within a unified retrieval framework.

Deepfake related harms expose a governance problem that cannot be resolved through criminalisation alone. Synthetic images, audio, and video can generate reputational, sexual, economic, privacy, and identity harms while circulating through infrastructures operated by multiple private and public actors. This study examines how Indonesia’s existing legal and public policy architecture addresses deepfake harms and develops an integrative digital governance model oriented toward prevention and victim protection. The research uses normative legal analysis with statutory, conceptual, policy, and limited comparative approaches. Primary materials include Indonesia’s Electronic Information and Transactions Law, Personal Data Protection Law, Criminal Code, Sexual Violence Crime Law, electronic system regulations, and national artificial intelligence policy instruments. Comparative lessons are drawn from the European Union’s AI transparency regime, Australia’s online safety model, and South Korea’s response to synthetic sexual abuse. The analysis finds that Indonesia possesses several applicable legal instruments, but they operate through separate legal interests, institutions, and remedial logics. This fragmentation leaves four governance deficits: weak ex ante authenticity safeguards, unclear platform due diligence standards, dispersed enforcement coordination, and victim remedies that are insufficiently rapid for viral synthetic content. The article proposes an Integrative Digital Governance framework consisting of prevention and authenticity, platform accountability, coordinated enforcement, and victim recovery. Its contribution lies in shifting Indonesian deepfake scholarship from offence by offence legal mapping toward a lifecycle-based governance architecture that connects regulation, institutional responsibility, technological safeguards, and measurable victim-centred outcomes.

The incorporation of artificial intelligence into accounting activities has generated new possibilities for process automation, information processing, and professional decision-making support. This study aimed to analyze the perception and use of artificial intelligence tools in accounting decision-making among professionals in Guayaquil. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional study was conducted through a survey administered to professionals working in accounting-related areas. From a population of 307 accountants approached, 222 valid responses were obtained through non-probability convenience sampling. The findings showed that 67.57% of participants considered that artificial intelligence tools improve the accuracy of accounting decisions, while 61.26% reported using them for this type of decision-making. Likewise, 76.58% indicated that these tools reduce the time required to make decisions. A statistically significant association was identified between age and willingness to use artificial intelligence, χ²(3) = 68.63, p < .001, with a Cramer's V of .56. The findings suggest that artificial intelligence has a favorable perception among the professionals studied, although its implementation requires training, human oversight, and ethical criteria.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: SignificanceIn recent years, the rapid advancement of industrial digitalization and intelligentization has extended the boundaries of cyberspace into the physical world, and urban rail transit systems, as critical national information infrastructure, have been exposed to increasingly severe cybersecurity threats. The network environment of urban rail industrial control systems is characterized by wide-area deployment, dynamic evolution, and strong heterogeneity. Extensive network coverage, dynamically changing operating conditions, and diverse equipment types and communication protocols impose higher requirements on the timeliness, accuracy, adaptability, and coordination capabilities of cybersecurity defenses. Conventional cybersecurity defenses often lack sufficient awareness and remain reactive in these environments, making timely and accurate discovery and identification of wide-area network threats difficult. Static and passive protection mechanisms cannot be readily adjusted to changes in network conditions and threats, while unified management and coordination of heterogeneous cybersecurity devices remain insufficient. Consequently, limited accuracy and timeliness in threat monitoring, static and passive defense mechanisms, and weak unified management and coordination capabilities remain major technical challenges. These challenges are further complicated by the interconnection of control centers, stations, train networks, and cloud platforms, through which threats may be propagated across different operational domains. Meanwhile, strict requirements for train operation safety, real-time control, and service continuity must be satisfied during security monitoring and defensive operations. Timely threat discovery must therefore be reconciled with accurate identification, and defensive policies must be adapted to changing network conditions and threat patterns. Research on artificial immunity and large language models is consequently needed to support the recognition of unfamiliar threats, the dynamic optimization of defensive policies, and the coordinated management of heterogeneous cybersecurity devices.ProgressTo address these challenges, artificial immunity and large language models were incorporated into a research framework for complex urban rail industrial control networks. Timely and accurate wide-area threat discovery, proactive defense against dynamically evolving threats, and collaborative orchestration of heterogeneous cybersecurity devices were identified as the three principal research problems. Three core techniques together with an integrated prototype system were included in the proposed framework. Specifically, an artificial-immune-recognition-based risk monitoring method was proposed to enable rapid threat detection and precise identification. Multisource heterogeneous data were considered for feature fusion and representation in a unified immune feature space. Traffic, logs, alerts, protocol commands, and equipment states were included among the information sources. Hierarchical clustering and detector tolerance training were incorporated into the detector generation scheme, and rapid responses within detector clusters were proposed to improve monitoring efficiency. A dual-verification mechanism was introduced, in which preliminary screening with self detectors was followed by further identification with non-self detectors. An artificial-immune-evolution-based proactive defense framework was then proposed to enhance protection against persistent and multistage attacks. Clonal proliferation and hierarchical differential evolution were incorporated into threat gene evolution to support the exploration of potential threat patterns. Stochastic attack-defense games and deep learning were combined in the proposed technical route for defense policy generation and adaptive dynamic optimization. Successive states, available actions, immediate rewards and costs, and expected future returns were considered in the game-based modeling of attack-defense interactions. A large-language-model-based collaborative management approach was also presented to coordinate diverse security devices for joint defense. Heterogeneous threat intelligence was organized within a cloud-edge-endpoint architecture for collection, aggregation, compression, and storage. The knowledge reasoning and generation capabilities of large language models were incorporated into intelligence analysis and the generation of cross-domain coordination plans. Risk monitoring systems, proactive defense systems, firewalls, and cryptographic appliances were included among the intended managed devices. Policy consistency checks, coordinated distribution, execution verification, and audit records were incorporated into the system design. Building upon this foundation, a prototype intelligent cybersecurity defense architecture was presented for urban rail transit systems, and system integration, deployment arrangements, and technical validation were outlined.Conclusions and ProspectsAn integrated research framework was proposed for cybersecurity defense in urban rail transit systems, with risk monitoring, proactive defense, and coordinated device management connected through three complementary technical directions. Artificial immune recognition was introduced for timely threat discovery and accurate identification, immune evolution was incorporated into adaptive defense policy generation, and large language models were introduced for heterogeneous threat intelligence analysis and collaborative device management. A technical route beyond traditional patch-based passive defense was thereby outlined to support the secure and reliable operation of national critical information infrastructure. Further research should be directed toward the adaptation of these techniques to actual urban rail operating conditions. Dynamic self-boundary modeling and unknown-threat recognition should be refined in response to changes in operating schedules, equipment conditions, and maintenance activities. Defense policy generation and optimization should be investigated under the constraints of train operation safety, real-time control, and service continuity. The explainability and traceability of generated management plans, cross-device policy consistency, and coordinated execution should also be strengthened. Prototype integration should be advanced, followed by system simulation, attack-defense evaluation, and third-party performance testing. Threat detection accuracy, response latency, dynamic defense policy generation, and coordinated handling across multiple devices should be evaluated, and application feedback should be used to refine the proposed technologies and methods.

Against the backdrop of population aging and the widespread adoption of digital technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into home- and community-based eldercare. However, many older adults continue to face a digital divide, while smart eldercare products often provide only superficial age-friendly adaptations and fail to match users' needs. This study examines older residents of urban communities and their family members. Drawing on a literature review, a questionnaire survey, and semi-structured interviews, it investigates the development of AI-enabled smart eldercare services and the difficulties older adults encounter when using smart devices and related services. Informed by digital divide theory, active aging theory, and supply-and-demand matching theory, the study analyzes the factors underlying these difficulties and proposes a smart eldercare service model that uses age-friendly short videos as a delivery medium and intergenerational collaboration as its core mechanism. It further develops operational strategies across six dimensions: content, target groups, channels, technology, implementation, and operations. Survey findings are used to assess the model's feasibility. The proposed approach offers communities and social organizations a low-cost, practical framework for more inclusive smart eldercare services, with the aim of narrowing the digital divide and supporting active aging.
topics: Aging, Elder Care, and Social Issues

documents.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can now produce fluent text, realistic images and convincing audio at almost no cost, and it does so without any commitment to truth. This has created a crisis of digital integrity: fabricated content is hard to distinguish from authentic content, machine outputs present invented claims as fact, and it is unclear who should answer for the resulting harm. Mainstream AI ethics has responded with principles such as transparency and accountability, but these frameworks draw mainly on Western philosophical traditions and treat deception largely as a technical or regulatory problem. Islamic scholarship on AI has grown quickly, yet most of it addresses AI in general through maqasid al-shariah, and its treatment of misinformation relies almost entirely on the receiver's duty of tabayyun (verification). This concept paper critically analyses truth, deception and responsibility in generative AI through Islamic ethics. Using conceptual analysis and theory adaptation, it synthesises the empirical literature on synthetic media with Qur'anic, prophetic and juristic concepts. It argues that Islamic ethics offers an integrated account built on three pillars: sidq (truthfulness) as a duty owed by every speaker and publisher, the prohibition of ghish, tadlis and kadhib (deception, concealment and falsehood) as limits on design and deployment, and amanah and mas'uliyyah (trust and answerability) as a model of responsibility that always returns to a human agent. The paper proposes a Digital Integrity Framework that distributes these duties across developers, deployers, users and regulators, and offers suggestions for policy, education and future research.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Recent studies of Policy Advisory Systems (PAS) focus on the quality of advice and how it is designed and managed. This article extends this analysis looking at the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on advisory systems’ behaviour and activity using Geoffrey Vickers’ concept of policy judgment. It notes how negligible user costs combined with the apparent robustness of AI computational outputs can generate advice that can exercise an important and independent influence on policy decisions and outcomes, despite that advice not always being accurate or well-considered. In this sense AI-generated advice shares some of the same characteristics of earlier mechanical algorithms framing policy problems and recommendations for action which lack the hallmarks of careful appreciation of the issues at stake. This is illustrated by the use of AI tools by the US Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) in 2025-2026, in particular its directive to autonomously reduce the number and size of contracts and grants made by many Departments, and specifically the US Department of Veterans Affairs. The case underlines that a crucial design challenge for AI-based policy advice is to go beyond only trying to ensure human oversight or a ‘Human-in-the-Loop’ in order to ensure that problems are properly articulated and actions towards them are sound.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: The presence of artificial intelligence (AI) and social media has transformed Generation Z’s patterns of learning, information seeking, and everyday interaction. However, previous research findings have not yielded consistent conclusions regarding the effects of these two technologies on critical thinking skills, while studies interpreting them through Paulo Freire’s critical education perspective remain limited. This study aims to analyze the partial and simultaneous effects of AI use and social media use intensity on Generation Z’s critical thinking skills and to interpret the results from Paulo Freire’s perspective. The study employed a quantitative approach with an explanatory survey design involving 100 Generation Z respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using an online questionnaire and analyzed through multiple linear regression with the assistance of SPSS. The findings indicate that AI use had no significant partial effect on critical thinking skills (p = 0.416), nor did the intensity of social media use (p = 0.198). Simultaneously, the two variables also had no significant effect on critical thinking skills (p = 0.435) and explained only 1.7% of the variation in these skills (R² = 0.017). These findings are consistent with Paulo Freire’s thought, which positions dialogue, reflection, and praxis as the primary elements in developing critical thinking skills rather than technology alone. This study concludes that AI and social media are not direct determinants of critical thinking skills but rather learning tools whose benefits depend on how users utilize, evaluate, and reflect on information. Theoretically, this study enriches educational research in the digital era by integrating Freire’s critical education perspective. Practically, these findings emphasize the importance of reflective learning, information verification, and dialogical methods in developing Generation Z’s critical thinking skills.

EN This thesis examines the theoretical, methodological, and practical aspects of applying artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning technologies to the assessment of customers' creditworthiness in commercial bank lending activities. The predictive performance of traditional scoring models (Logistic Regression) and modern AI algorithms (XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, Neural Networks) is comparatively analyzed using ROC-AUC and Gini indicators. The thesis also discusses the use of alternative Big Data sources, the processing of transactional and textual data, and Explainable AI (XAI) and SHAP approaches aimed at mitigating the "black box" problem of artificial intelligence. Based on the findings, practical recommendations are proposed for introducing AI-based credit scoring mechanisms into the national banking system. This study examined the relationship between leadership practices and employee motivation among construction workers employed by selected tenant general contractors in a medium-scale commercial project in Santa Rosa, Laguna, Philippines, as a basis for developing a Workforce Engagement Program. Anchored in Full-Range Leadership Theory and Self-Determination Theory, the study employed a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design involving 63 construction workers from five tenant general contractors selected through total enumeration. Data were collected using an expert-validated structured survey questionnaire and analyzed using frequency, percentage, weighted mean, and Pearson product-moment correlation. Findings revealed that most respondents had limited construction experience and relatively short company tenure. Leadership practices were generally perceived positively, with supervisory support receiving the highest weighted mean (3.76), while recognition and appreciation received the lowest (2.82), indicating weaknesses in formal monetary and non-monetary recognition. Employee motivation was generally high, particularly intrinsic motivation (3.72), followed by professional growth (3.58) and extrinsic motivation (3.57). However, the relationship between leadership practices and employee motivation was statistically nonsignificant (r = −0.022, p = 0.864). The study proposed KILOS-KAPWA: A Construction Workforce Engagement and Recognition Program to strengthen supervisory communication, employee recognition, professional development, workplace support, and participatory decision-making. The findings align with Sustainable Development Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and Sustainable Development Goal 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure). The proposed program may contribute to organizational and socioeconomic sustainability by supporting workforce engagement, employee development, and responsible construction workforce management, although its effectiveness requires evaluation following implementation.

Deploying generative artificial intelligence and deep computer vision architectures into production environments requires overcoming strict hardware memory ceilings, cloud API rate throttling, structural output hallucinations, and real-time latency bounds. This paper presents a unified empirical study of three production-grade artificial intelligence systems engineered specifically for resource-constrained execution across local workstations, cloud-hybrid inference pipelines, and edge vision monitors: (1) A privacy-first, local multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture utilizing 384-dimensional sentence transformers dense embeddings indexed inside an embedded sqlite-vec engine, a dual-layer visual inference router failing over automatically from cloud Qwen 27B (via the Featherless API) to a locally hosted Moondream vision-language model, and a memory-bounded local phi3 inference engine via Ollama constrained to a strict 4,096-token context ceiling to guarantee a 0% out-of-memory (OOM) crash rate; (2) An end-to-end Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation, post-training alignment via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and feedback intelligence framework benchmarking Aspect-Based, Few-Shot, and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting strategies to achieve 99.5% classification accuracy and a 90% reduction in end-to-end processing latency, sustained by a stateful Dynamic API Key Rotation middleware that bypasses the 15 Requests-Per-Minute (15 RPM) free-tier Google Gemini API rate ceiling, alongside deterministic JSON tool-calling schema verification and multimodal reasoning fine-tuning on VEO-3 and Gemini; and (3) A real-time computer vision safety and industrial inspection suite comprising a hybrid ResNet-50 and dlib Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) ensemble for driver microsleep detection (achieving 92% classification accuracy, 35% fewer false positive alerts, and strictly < 100 ms per-frame inference latency across 10,000+ video frames) paired with an OpenCV and TensorFlow-Keras Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) predictive maintenance pipeline for micro-tool wear classification across 5,000+ augmented images (expanded 100× from 50+ base microscopy images) and 100+ milling intervals using 3 extracted morphological wear descriptors (achieving 75% multi-class classification accuracy).

Long-acting injectables (LAIs) are innovative drug-delivery systems allowing for prolonged controlled release of a drug after a single administration. By decreasing the dosing frequency, long-acting injectable can have a positive impact on treatment compliance, patient convenience, and drug exposure while minimising the peak–trough fluctuations. This review provides an overview of the different formulation approaches used to develop LAIs, including microspheres, Nano crystal suspensions, oil-based depots, in situ forming depots, implants, hydrogels, lyotropic liquid crystalline systems, polymer-lipid hybrids, and modified protein and peptide therapeutics. The review highlights the main advantages and limitations of LAIs, such as patient adherence and consistent drug exposure, while also discussing injection site reactions, prolonged drug exposure, challenges of flexible dose adjustment, manufacturing complexity, and cost. Storage requirements will be discussed. The clinical applications in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, HIV treatment and prevention, opioid use disorder, growth hormone deficiency, and diabetes. Ophthalmic diseases will be highlighted together with the marketed products in each therapeutic area. Finally, emerging technologies, patient-friendly LAI approaches, biomaterials, artificial intelligence, predictive modelling, and personalised medicine are discussed. In conclusion, LAIs are an important class of drug delivery systems that can have a significant impact on optimal and sustained drug exposure while decreasing the treatment burden on the patient. The complexity of the different formulation approaches and the need for clinical development expertise are still major hurdles that industry is currently trying to address by developing new approaches and manufacturing processes.

The ability to form healthy attachments with others has long been established to be important for mental health and well-being. The Experiences in Close Relationships-Revised Scale (Fraley et al., 2000) identifies two dimensions of attachment - model of self (attachment anxiety; degree to which an individual worries about rejection, abandonment, or unworthiness of love), and model of other (attachment avoidance; degree to which an individual fears emotional intimacy, suppresses dependency, and insists upon behavioral self-reliance). However, less is understood about whether the impact of attachment spills over in the academic lives of college students. The current study examines whether academic performance (GPA) and/or academic motivation (subscales in the Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire; Pintrich et al., 1991) is predictive of attachment in college students (N = 112). Separate multiple linear regression analyses will be conducted to examine if GPA and/or subscales of academic motivation (intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, task value, control of learning beliefs, self-efficacy for learning and performance, and test anxiety) can predict attachment (model of self and model of other). Understanding whether academic performance and/or academic motivation is predictive of attachment styles is fundamental to understanding the value of social connections in academic settings. Such insights can aid institutions in tailoring guidance to help students reach their full academic potential. Keywords: attachment styles, academic performance, academic motivation

Abstract Background Preoperative neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is associated with short-term outcomes after cardiac surgery, but its value for long-term mortality prediction remains unclear. We developed a machine learning model incorporating NLR to predict 10-year all-cause mortality after cardiac surgery, and used explainable artificial intelligence to interpret the role of NLR. Methods We included adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery from the MIMIC-IV database. The primary outcome was 10-year all-cause mortality. Six machine learning models were compared using grid search, stratified 5-fold cross-validation, and bootstrap internal validation. The best model was interpreted using SHAP on the test set. The NLR cutoff was identified by piecewise regression on the training set. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance. Results Among 4,891 patients (median age 68 years), 222 (4.54%) died within 10 years. After tuning, XGBoost performed best (optimism-corrected AUC = 0.815; 95% CI: 0.758–0.861), outperforming LASSO regression (AUC = 0.780). NLR alone had an AUC of 0.709, similar to APACHE III (0.732; P = 0.630). Combining NLR with APACHE III improved the AUC to 0.761 (P = 0.002). SHAP analysis identified APACHE III (0.371) and NLR (0.291) as the top two predictors. Piecewise regression identified an NLR cutoff of 6.5. At a 15% risk threshold, the positive predictive value was 23.3% (5.1-fold enrichment). Decision curve analysis showed net benefit across thresholds of 5%-30%. Conclusions Preoperative NLR is an independent predictor of 10-year mortality after cardiac surgery, with performance comparable to APACHE III. The tuned XGBoost model showed good overall performance. An NLR threshold of 6.5 was identified and supported by SHAP analysis. NLR may complement existing risk scores for long-term risk stratification, but should not be used as a standalone tool.

Teacher human resource quality improvement management is an important aspect of efforts to improve the quality of education in schools. This study aims to analyze teacher human resource quality improvement management in improving the quality of education at SMA Negeri 1 Pamekasan. This study used a descriptive qualitative approach involving the principal, vice principal for curriculum affairs, teachers, and school documentation as data sources. Data were collected through interviews, observation, and documentation, then analyzed through the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. Data validity was confirmed through source triangulation and technique triangulation. The results show that teacher quality improvement was carried out through needs-based planning by utilizing SWOT analysis and the education report card, as well as the implementation of various development programs, such as In-House Training (IHT), MGMP, supervision, technology training, and the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in learning. Teacher quality improvement contributed to more active learning, increased student creativity and achievement, and improved school education report card results. However, its implementation still faced challenges in the form of technological adaptation and resistance to change among senior teachers. This study contributes to the development of educational human resource management studies, particularly in strengthening teacher quality as a strategic factor in improving school quality. The implications of this study emphasize the importance of teacher development planning that is needs-based, sustainable, and responsive to the transformation of learning technology.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in strategic decision-making, competitive positioning, innovation management, organizational learning, and governance, yet the literature remains fragmented across management, information systems, innovation, and technology-management fields. This study provides a focused bibliometric review of AI research in strategic management. Scopus was used as the primary database, and the query "artificial intelligence" AND "strategic management" was applied to titles, abstracts, and keywords, with restrictions to Business, Management and Accounting, Article and Review document types, and English-language publications. From 126 retrieved records, relevance screening excluded 82 records, leaving 44 publications for analysis. The study examines annual trends, citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, country distribution, science maps, TCCM synthesis, and a WoS/SSCI sensitivity analysis. Results show slow development before 2018 and marked acceleration after 2023, with 2026 treated as an incomplete year. Themes are shifting from decision support and strategic planning toward generative AI, innovation management, sustainability, organizational capabilities, and governance. By combining bibliometric mapping, TCCM, and cross-database sensitivity analysis, this study offers a knowledge-structure map and future research agenda.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: This study applies a refined model of Artificial Intelligence (AI) integration into Academic Quality Management Systems (AQMS) within South African private higher education. It builds on prior validation through exploratory factor analysis and reliability testing to examine how institutional factors relate to stakeholders’ perceptions of AI integration. Survey data from higher education and education technology stakeholders were analysed using PLS-SEM, correlation, multiple regression, and descriptive statistics. The results show moderate explanatory power, with regression indicating stronger overall model performance than PLS-SEM. Across analyses, Research Governance and Responsible AI Use emerged as the most consistent and statistically supported factor associated with AI_QMS. Strategic Planning and AI in Teaching and Learning also contributed positively, although their effects varied by method. In contrast, AI Literacy and Competency Development and Assessment and Evaluation produced inconsistent results, including negative regression coefficients, which are interpreted cautiously due to shared variance and measurement limitations. Other factors, including Ethical Considerations and Data Privacy, Environmental Impact, and Interdisciplinary Collaboration, did not demonstrate independent explanatory power in multivariable models. The findings highlight that observable institutional activity does not necessarily translate into consistent integration within academic quality systems. The study contributes a multi-dimensional framework that distinguishes between strongly supported relationships, method-dependent effects, and areas requiring further measurement development. Practically, the model provides institutions with a structured approach to assess and strengthen AI integration within academic quality management.

This work investigates the impact of data drift on machine learning models deployed for Human Activity Recognition (HAR) using the UCI Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones dataset. A Random Forest classifier is trained on an initial stable data distribution using a chronological split to reflect real-world deployment conditions. Model performance is first evaluated under no-drift conditions to establish a baseline. To study degradation, data drift is simulated by injecting Gaussian noise into the sensor features of future data, representing realistic changes such as sensor noise and calibration shifts. This controlled perturbation leads to a measurable decline in classification accuracy, precision, and recall, demonstrating the vulnerability of static models to evolving data distributions. Model degradation is monitored using the ADWIN (Adaptive Windowing) drift detection algorithm applied to the prediction error stream, enabling automatic identification of statistically significant performance changes. To mitigate degradation, a sliding-window retraining strategy is applied using recent samples, resulting in partial recovery of model performance. The results highlight the importance of time-aware evaluation, drift detection, and lightweight retraining for maintaining reliable machine learning systems in dynamic and resource-constrained environments.

The objective of this scoping review was to map the existing scientific literature on the relationship between motivations and constraints for playing digital games and esports, characterizing study profiles, identifying dominant themes and tensions, and examining the extent to which their interaction has been theorized and empirically investigated. Following Arksey and O'Malley’s framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a search across EBSCO, SCOPUS, and Web of Science identified 38 eligible studies published between 1985 and 2025. The findings reveal a profound structural and theoretical imbalance: research is heavily skewed toward motivation-driven "pull factors" (76.3 %), while constraints remain critically understudied (13.2 %). Crucially, integrative studies (10.5 %) demonstrate that while intrinsic motivations can mitigate logistical barriers, deep psychosocial and symbolic constraints rooted in identity exclusion and social stigma consistently override motivation, triggering disengagement or severe affective costs. This review exposes the theoretical limitations of isolated psychological models, arguing for integrative, socio-culturally sensitive frameworks capable of capturing motivations and constraints as interdependent dynamics of the situated gaming experience.

Benefiting from recent advances in generative AI and large language models (LLMs), current LLM-driven AI systems are rapidly reshaping how we reason, plan, and make decisions. Yet endowing these systems with human-like temporal intelligence (e.g., understanding and comparing events across time) remains largely unresolved. To address this gap, we introduce a novel Multi-dimensional Hierarchical Temporal Alignment framework (denoted as MHTA), of which the core idea is to effectively ground the temporal alignment of an LLM in both event-specific and cross-event real-world temporal commonsense knowledge. Specifically, we first frame the temporal space as a multi-dimensional hierarchical space, where each dimension comprises its own set of temporal units. Building on this formulation, we curate an initial burn-in dataset in which annotations are constructed to reflect real-world human temporal commonsense in accordance with our defined temporal space. Based on the initial burn-in dataset, we propose two complementary fine-tuning objectives: (i) Grounding the temporal alignment in event-specific temporal commonsense knowledge, which is achieved through a novel hierarchy-preserving Wasserstein loss, and (ii) Grounding the temporal alignment in cross-event temporal commonsense knowledge, which is achieved via a margin-adaptive triplet loss. To evaluate the effectiveness of MHTA, we conduct extensive experiments on three representative benchmarks (MCTACO, DurationQA, and TimeDial). For example, on the MCTACO dataset, MHTA improves Mistral-7B by 6.0% in accuracy and 10.3% in exact match, and improves DeepSeek-LLM-7B by 5.4% in accuracy and 9.8% in exact match. Combined with different backbones, MHTA surpasses nearly all baselines across the three benchmarks and exceeds the performance of advanced models such as GPT-4o on MCTACO and DurationQA. These results demonstrate that MHTA provides consistent gains in temporal commonsense reasoning across diverse LLM backbones.

This study compares how young adults make rapid online reaching corrections following either physical or visual perturbations, and whether cognitive abilities predict corrective motor performance. Sixty-one participants completed an obstacle avoidance reaching task using a robotic interface that introduced either force-based physical perturbations or visually displaced cursor feedback and completed measures of cognitive performance. Behavioral analyses showed that collision rates did not differ between perturbation modalities; however, movement corrections following visual perturbations were significantly slower than those following physical, particularly when participants navigated around obstacles. Participants were also more likely to select outward corrective paths during physical perturbations. Regression analyses demonstrated that processing speed, psychomotor speed, and executive control predicted corrective movement performance, with stronger cognitive associations observed for visual perturbations. These findings suggest that although both perturbation types rely on shared corrective motor processes, responses to visual perturbations require greater cortical and cognitive involvement than responses to physical perturbations.

Transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) provide several advantages over conventional oral and parenteral routes, including avoidance of gastrointestinal degradation and hepatic first-pass metabolism, improved patient compliance, and controlled drug delivery. However, the stratum corneum acts as a major barrier, limiting the passive transport of hydrophilic and high-molecular-weight therapeutic agents. This review focuses on recent advances in polymeric microneedles and nanocarrier-mediated transdermal drug delivery systems developed to overcome these skin-permeation limitations. Literature from PubMed and Scopus was reviewed with emphasis on microneedle classification, polymeric biomaterials, nanocarrier systems, drug-loading capacity, permeation mechanisms, safety, and clinical translation. Polymeric microneedles, including solid, coated, dissolving, hydrogel-forming, and hollow systems, enable controlled and minimally painful delivery by creating temporary microchannels through the stratum corneum. Nanocarriers such as liposomes, ethosomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, nanostructured lipid carriers, polymeric nanoparticles, and inorganic nanoparticles further enhance dermal and transdermal drug transport through lipid fluidization, follicular pathways, and controlled drug deposition. The integration of these technologies provides promising opportunities for delivering macromolecules, vaccines, and localized therapeutics. Future developments involving stimuli-responsive systems, wearable biosensors, artificial intelligence, microfluidics, and personalized manufacturing may further enhance transdermal therapy. Despite challenges related to manufacturing scalability, regulatory standardization, and long-term biocompatibility, advanced microneedle and nanocarrier platforms have considerable potential for clinical translation and personalized drug delivery. Background: Traditional transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) provide a non-invasive, patient-compliant route that avoids gastrointestinal degradation and hepatic first-pass metabolism. However, the impermeable lipid matrix of the stratum corneum strictly limits the passive transport of molecules to those possessing specific hydrophobic profiles and low molecular weights. Objective: This comprehensive review examines contemporary physical and chemical breakthrough technologies, with specific focus on polymeric microneedles (MNs) and nanocarrier-facilitated delivery platforms engineered to overcome these macro-molecular transport constraints. Methodology: A systematic screening of literature from the PubMed and Scopus databases (spanning foundational models through 2026) was conducted to evaluate the mechanical structural properties, biopolymer selections, and systemic pharmacokinetics of advanced skin-permeation platforms. Results: Polymeric microneedles (dissolving, hydrogel-forming, and stimuli-responsive types) demonstrate precise disruption of the stratum corneum without contacting dermally located pain-sensitive nerve endings. Concurrently, lipidic, polymeric, and inorganic nanocarriers capitalize on hair follicles and transient lipid fluidization to deposit high-molecular-weight biologics, vaccines, and localized therapeutics. Conclusion: Combining active mechanical microneedles with target-specific nanocarriers represents the vanguard of modern personalized diagnostics and therapeutics, bridging laboratory innovation with clinical scale-up paradigms.

Novokult LLM is a desktop application that runs a large language model on your own computer. It is built for left-wing organizers, researchers, and writers. Once a model file is on your machine, drafting, analysis, and chat can stay there. It has three modes: analysis of events and texts through a Marxist framework, agitprop drafting (leaflets, slogans, speeches, songs, strike bulletins), and free chat. You can load your own texts as a Sources Library, turn on web search routed through Tor, and export posters. The design starts from an argument. AI is machinery, and most of it is rented from a few firms that see every prompt. Novokult runs the machine where its users live and work, and its code is published under the Peer Production License, a copyfarleft license meant to keep it in common. The title of this paper names the older question behind that choice: who builds a movement's culture, and with what tools. The name Novokult contracts the Russian новая культура (novaya kultura), "new culture." Version 1.0.0 is built for Windows (portable and installer) and Linux (AppImage and deb). An Android port exists in the code but is unfinished.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Occupational exposure to airborne pollutants poses a significant risk to hematological health. This systematic review aims to evaluate the associations between workplace airborne pollutants and key blood parameters, as well as the modifying roles of age and body mass index (BMI) among adult industrial workers. Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive search across Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Medline identified studies published over the last five decades. The search strategy incorporated terms related to occupational air pollution and airborne pollutants, including particulate matter (PM), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and heavy metals (HMs). Studies evaluating occupational exposures and reporting hematological outcomes-hemoglobin concentration, mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH), mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC), and anemia prevalence-were included. Methodological quality was assessed using study design-specific JBI critical appraisal checklists. Out of 1855 retrieved records, 55 studies (predominantly from developing and industrializing countries) met the eligibility criteria. Findings reveal that workplace exposure to VOCs, HMs (e.g., lead), and PM is consistently associated with subclinical hematological alterations, characterized by lower hemoglobin levels and altered red blood cell indices (MCH and MCHC). Notably, despite high workplace pollutant concentrations, linear correlations between pollutant levels and hematological indices were often weak, indicating complex exposure-response dynamics. Analysis of modifying factors showed that higher BMI was positively associated with hemoglobin levels, potentially suggesting a protective buffering pattern, whereas age exhibited weak associations, likely reflecting a "healthy-worker effect" in exposed populations. The complexity of these findings underscores the necessity of moving beyond single-pollutant assessments toward evaluating mixed workplace exposures. Integrating routine hematological surveillance and nutritional screening into occupational health programs is crucial for mitigating workplace hematotoxicity.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Ushbu tadqiqot oliy ta'lim muassasalarida (OTM) sun'iy intellekt (SI) ekotizimini shakllantirish va uning ta'lim samaradorligi hamda sifat koʻrsatkichlariga ta'sirini konseptual va empirik jihatdan baholashga bagʻishlangan. Tadqiqotda aralash metodologiya (mixed-methods design), xususan, strukturaviy tenglamalarni modellashtirish (PLS-SEM), empirik soʻrovnoma hamda LMS (Learning Management System) platformalarining log-fayllari ma'lumotlariga tayangan holda koʻp omilli ekonometrik modellashtirish usuli qoʻllanilgan. Natijalar SI ekotizimining individual adaptiv oʻqitish va kognitiv koʻnikmalarni rivojlantirish orqali talabalarning akademik oʻzlashtirishiga statistik jihatdan ahamiyatli va ijobiy ta'sir koʻrsatishini, shuningdek, professor-oʻqituvchilarning raqamli-pedagogik kompetensiyasi ushbu bogʻliqlikda moderatsiyalovchi rol oʻynashini koʻrsatdi. Tadqiqot natijalari asosida OTMlarda SI konvergensiyasi va institutsional transformatsiyaning konseptual freymvorki ishlab chiqilgan. EN This study is devoted to the conceptual and empirical assessment of the formation of an artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem in higher education institutions (HEIs) and its impact on educational efficiency and quality indicators. The study employs a mixed-methods design, including Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), empirical survey data, and log-file data from Learning Management System (LMS) platforms, within a multivariate econometric modeling framework. The results indicate that the AI ecosystem has a statistically significant and positive effect on students' academic performance through individualized adaptive learning and the development of cognitive skills. The findings also show that the digital-pedagogical competence of academic staff plays a moderating role in this relationship. Based on the research results, a conceptual framework for AI convergence and institutional transformation in higher education institutions has been developed. RU Исследование посвящено концептуальной и эмпирической оценке формирования экосистемы искусственного интеллекта (ИИ) в высших образовательных учреждениях и её влияния на показатели эффективности и качества образования. В исследовании применена смешанная методология (mixed-methods design), включающая моделирование структурными уравнениями методом частичных наименьших квадратов (PLS-SEM), данные эмпирического опроса и лог-файлы платформ систем управления обучением (Learning Management System, LMS), а также методы многофакторного эконометрического моделирования. Результаты показывают, что экосистема ИИ оказывает статистически значимое положительное влияние на академическую lazizbekablazov@gmail.com успеваемость студентов посредством индивидуализированного адаптивного обучения и развития когнитивных навыков. Кроме того, установлено, что цифрово-педагогическая компетентность профессорско-преподавательского состава играет модерирующую роль в данной взаимосвязи. На основе результатов исследования разработан концептуальный фреймворк конвергенции ИИ и институциональной трансформации высших образовательных учреждений.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Mazkur maqolada zamonaviy bosqichda oliy ta'lim tizimini raqamli transformatsiya qilishning nazariymetodologik, texnologik va amaliy masalalari tadqiq etilgan. Oliy ta'lim muassasalarida raqamli ekotizimlarni yaratish, axborot-boshqaruv tizimlari (HEMIS, LMS), sun'iy intellekt (AI), moslashuvchan ta'lim (Adaptive Learning) va Big Data texnologiyalarini ta'lim jarayoniga integratsiya qilishning istiqbolli yoʻnalishlari yoritilgan. Shuningdek, raqamlashtirish jarayonida yuzaga kelayotgan tizimli masalalar — raqamli tafovut, professor-oʻqituvchilarning raqamli pedagogik kompetensiyalarini rivojlantirish zarurati va kiberxavfsizlik xatarlari tahlil qilingan. Tadqiqot natijalari asosida oliy ta'lim muassasalarini «Smart University» (Aqlli universitet) modeliga bosqichma-bosqich oʻtkazish va ta'lim sifatini oshirish boʻyicha ilmiy-amaliy taklif hamda tavsiyalar ishlab chiqilgan. EN This article examines the theoretical-methodological, technological, and practical aspects of the digital transformation of higher education at the current stage. It highlights promising directions for creating digital ecosystems in higher education institutions and integrating information management systems (HEMIS, LMS), artificial intelligence (AI), adaptive learning technologies, and Big Data into the educational process. The article also analyzes key systemic issues arising in the digitalization process, including the digital divide, the need to develop the digital pedagogical competencies of academic staff, and cybersecurity risks. Based on the research findings, scientific and practical proposals and recommendations are developed for the gradual transition of higher education institutions to the Smart University model and for improving the quality of education. RU В статье исследуются теоретико-методологические, технологические и практические аспекты цифровой трансформации системы высшего образования на современном этапе. Освещены перспективные направления создания цифровых экосистем в высших образовательных учреждениях, а также интеграции информационноуправленческих систем (HEMIS, LMS), искусственного интеллекта (AI), адаптивного обучения (Adaptive Learning) и технологий Big Data в образовательный процесс. Кроме того, проанализированы ключевые системные вопросы, возникающие в процессе цифровизации, включая цифровой разрыв, необходимость развития цифровых педагогических компетенций профессорско-преподавательского состава и риски кибербезопасности. На основе результатов исследования разработаны научно-практические предложения и рекомендации по поэтапному переходу высших образовательных учреждений к модели Smart University и повышению качества образования.

Z.-W. Sun conjectured (arXiv:2411.14308, Conjecture 5.5) that every integer n > 51 can be written as w(5w−1)/2 + x(5x−1)/2 + y(5y+1)/2 + z(5z+1)/2 with w, x, y, z natural numbers. We prove the stronger statement that every natural number n except n = 1 and n = 19 has such a representation. The problem reduces to finding lattice points on a sphere in a coset of 10Z⁴ with exactly two negative coordinates. We detect these with a degree-8 polynomial weight, and bound the resulting theta series of weights 2 to 10 and level 400 through explicit newform decompositions and Deligne's bound. This leaves 8,167,125 explicit integers below 10¹⁰, which are checked directly. The proof is computer-assisted: the decompositions are certified in ball arithmetic and the polynomial inequality in exact arithmetic. An independent audit by a separate AI run recomputed every step with different code and found no error. All modular-forms constants were also re-derived independently in SageMath, without PARI/GP, and every constant matched. An external review by ChatGPT found no objection to the main proof; its wording points have been corrected. No human expert has yet checked the argument. The mathematics, code and audits were produced by the AI system Claude (Anthropic) under the author's direction; see Section 8 of the paper. This record contains the paper, all programs, certificates, logs and the audit report.

This article investigates the complex problem of protecting human personal data during modern armed conflicts, particularly through the prism of hybrid warfare. The rapid pace of digitalization, the advancement of artificial intelligence technologies, and their active integration into the military sphere drive the relevance of this study. These factors cause fundamental changes in the methods and means of warfare, as well as in the very purpose of armed conflict. Today, informational influence and psychological pressure on the enemy's population - which are not always accompanied by a direct armed attack - constitute an integral component of any 21st-century military conflict. Consequently, the study analyzes the concept of hybrid warfare, defining it through characteristic features such as asymmetry, large-scale involvement of non-state actors, latency, and a combination of military and non-military means of struggle. The research specifically focuses on the role of generative artificial intelligence in the context of growing cyber threats. The paper emphasizes that unauthorized access to individuals' personal data during an armed conflict allows opposing parties to exert targeted psychological influence on population groups or individuals, manipulate public opinion through disinformation and «deepfakes,» and apply illegal filtration and terror against the population. Furthermore, this study analyzes the current international legal framework regarding personal data protection in conflict conditions. It examines the provisions of international humanitarian law, particularly the Fourth Geneva Convention of 1949. The findings establish that IHL norms lack special provisions for protecting digitized information. Moreover, ongoing discussions among researchers regarding the recognition of digital data as a «civilian object» significantly complicate the qualification of an enemy's actions in cyberspace as a violation of international humanitarian law. Finally, the article explores the provisions of specific international acts regulating data protection. The analysis determines that the permitted derogation from certain obligations in this sphere can lead to state abuses, often hidden behind the necessity of ensuring national security and defense. Ultimately, the paper highlights that international human rights law, through the provisions of international treaties and the case law of the ECtHR, establishes general guarantees to ensure compliance with the criteria of legality, strict necessity, and proportionality when interfering with the human right to personal data protection.

Agentic artificial intelligence is taking supply chain software from recommendation to execution. Planning and procurement agents now execute replenishment orders, reallocate freight, and negotiate with suppliers based on delegated powers, all without simultaneous human approval. Virtually every organization maintains the records of such activities as log files, subject only to IT retention policies until the files are no longer useful for diagnostic purposes and then disposed of. This opinion article contends that such treatment misclassifies what is, in substance, evidence of business transactions. An agent-executed decision that commits expenditure, alters a contractual position or redistributes risk across trading partners creates obligations that auditors, counterparties, regulators and courts may later test, and its trace therefore meets the functional definition of a record. Drawing on records continuum theory, the article follows a single agent decision across the dimensions of creation, capture, organisation and pluralisation and locates the points at which it leaves any recordkeeping regime. It then specifies the attributes of a trustworthy decision record in terms of reliability, authenticity and integrity, and proposes a governance arrangement in which records and information managers hold design authority over decision records alongside IT, procurement, legal and audit functions. The argument is addressed to information professionals in commercial settings who will increasingly be asked to evidence what an agent did, and on whose authority.

Temporal information in structured electronic health records (EHRs) is often lost in sparse one-hot or count-based representations, while sequence models can be costly and data-hungry. We propose PaReGTA, an LLM-based encoding framework that (i) converts longitudinal EHR events into visit-level templated text with explicit temporal cues, (ii) learns domain-adapted visit embeddings via lightweight contrastive fine-tuning of a sentence-embedding model, and (iii) aggregates visit embeddings into a fixed-dimensional patient representation using hybrid temporal pooling that captures both recency and globally informative visits. The resulting fixed-dimensional patient representations can be used with conventional downstream machine-learning models. To examine factor-level sensitivity, we use PaReGTA-RSS (Representation Shift Score), a prespecified factor-removal analysis that recomputes patient representations after removing clinically defined factor groups and quantifies the resulting change in the fitted logit of a fixed logistic-regression model. We evaluated PaReGTA in a cohort of 39 088 patients with migraine from the All of Us Research Program (AoU) on a retrospective patient-level classification task with an EHR-derived target. In an exploratory comparison on the fixed held-out test cohort of 7818 patients, PaReGTA-Gap + LightGBM, used as a post hoc analytical reference, had the highest reported AUC, accuracy, and F1 values among the evaluated sparse, BERT-based EHR, and recurrent approaches in this cohort.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in higher education has transformed the way students seek information, complete assignments, and understand academic materials. However, AI use also raises ethical issues, including plagiarism, overreliance on instant answers, and a lack of transparency in acknowledging AI assistance. This study aims to analyze the effect of digital literacy on the ethical use of AI among university students. A quantitative survey method was employed. Data were collected using a 1–5 Likert-scale questionnaire from 125 respondents, with 119 complete responses analyzed. Digital literacy was measured using 12 items, while ethical AI use was measured using 12 items. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, validity testing, reliability testing, correlation, and simple linear regression. The results show that digital literacy has a positive and significant effect on ethical AI use. The correlation coefficient of 0.638 indicates a strong relationship, while the coefficient of determination of 0.406 indicates that digital literacy explains 40.6% of the variation in ethical AI use. The regression equation is Y = 1.196 + 0.706X. These findings indicate that students with higher digital literacy tend to use AI more ethically, responsibly, and transparently. This study recommends strengthening digital literacy programs with an emphasis on AI ethics in higher education.

topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Teachers’ health and well-being are essential for promoting positive educational environments and healthy lifestyles within schools. Emotional intelligence and physical self-concept have emerged as relevant psychological factors associated with engagement in physical activity; however, evidence among secondary education teachers remains limited. The objective of this study was to analyse the relationships between physical activity, trait emotional intelligence and perceived physical self-concept among secondary education teachers, as well as to examine the indirect association between emotional intelligence and physical activity through physical self-concept. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 85 secondary education teachers from schools in the Region of Murcia (Spain). Participants completed the Trait Emotional Intelligence Questionnaire-Short Form (TEIQue-SF), the Physical Self-Concept Questionnaire (PSQ), and a physical activity assessment based on the PACE questionnaire. Descriptive analyses, Pearson correlations, MANOVA, and structural equation modelling were performed. Physical activity was positively associated with all dimensions of physical self-concept and with the sociability dimension of emotional intelligence. Teachers reporting higher levels of physical activity showed more favourable perceptions of their physical competence, condition, strength and self-esteem. In an exploratory structural equation model, emotional intelligence was positively associated with physical self-concept, which in turn was associated with physical activity; the indirect effect of emotional intelligence on physical activity through physical self-concept was significant (β = .18; 95% bootstrap CI [.03, .42]) and the direct effect was non-significant, a pattern statistically consistent with mediation that requires longitudinal confirmation. Physical activity is associated with better physical self-perceptions and greater emotional resources among secondary education teachers. These findings highlight the potential value of promoting active lifestyles within educational settings as a strategy to enhance teachers’ well-being and occupational health. Future longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the causal relationships among these variables.

Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the teaching and learning of second language (L2) writing. Despite AI's affordances in assisting L2 writing, improvements in writing skills and learning outcomes that extend beyond producing polished texts largely depend on students' active AI engagement, typically involving AI‐generated content and AI tools. This study adopts a qualitative, classroom‐based inquiry to examine how 56 L2 postgraduate students engage with AI in an authentic academic writing class. Framing engagement as a multidimensional meta‐construct, we identify a contextualized pattern of engagement characterized by students' agential role in shaping human–AI interactions across behavioral, cognitive, emotional, and social dimensions. Specifically, behavioral engagement occurs at compositional and operational levels, whereas cognitive engagement involves cognitive autonomy and metacognitive awareness. Students' emotional engagement involves appreciation and relief, as well as caution and emotional distance. Social engagement intersects with other dimensions, potentially shaping how students act, think, and feel in relation to AI through collaborative reflection. The findings inform a reconceptualization of engagement as a fluid, situated process, moving beyond a simple engagement–disengagement dichotomy toward a dynamic continuum shaped by the ongoing interplay across its multiple dimensions, encompassing both synergies and tensions. Implications for L2 writing and learning are also discussed.

Objectives: This study examined the educational outcomes of a credit-based internship program for third-year university students majoring in Medical Sciences, focusing on changes in their Fundamental Skills for Working Adults and career awareness. Methods: Participants were 57 third-year students from the Faculty of Medical Sciences at University A enrolled in a credit-based internship course. On completion of the internship, a web-based questionnaire was administered. The survey included self-evaluations of Fundamental Skills for Working Adults, Likert scales to evaluate subjective learning outcomes, and open-ended responses. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative data were categorized using qualitative content analysis. Results: Forty-two students responded to the questionnaire (response rate: 73.7%). For Fundamental Skills for Working Adults, more than 80% reported improvements in Proactivity, Active Listening, Situational Awareness, and Discipline. Subjective evaluations showed high overall satisfaction, with 97.6% of respondents reporting being either "very satisfied" or "satisfied," and 95.2% reporting changes in future vision and career awareness. Qualitative analysis yielded five categories, including "multifaceted understanding of medical settings and workplaces" and "concretization of career visions." Conclusion: Credit-based internships can effectively contribute to the development of Fundamental Skills for Working Adults and enhance career awareness among Medical Sciences students.

Unexpected machine failures can interrupt production, increase repair expenses, and create safety risks. Predictive machine maintenance usessensor data, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Machine Learning (ML) to estimate when equipment may develop a fault. Instead of servicing every machine atfixed intervals or waiting for a breakdown, the system continuously monitors parameters such as vibration, temperature, pressure, current, and operating hours.Data is cleaned and analysed, and a trained ML model identifies abnormal behaviour or predicts the remaining useful life of a component. The system can thengenerate an alert so that maintenance is planned before failure occurs. This paper explains the concept, working process, major technologies, model design,applications, benefits, limitations, and a practical implementation framework. It also discusses data quality, model evaluation, cybersecurity, and humanverification.
